sections.h2: Which Heard County tax office to call first
sections.html:
Two rooms in the Administration Building in Franklin split the work. Room 300 takes payments. Room 400 sets parcel values and approves exemptions. Walking into the wrong one costs an afternoon.

Heard County tax offices at the Franklin administration building
OfficeAddress and mailPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner201 Park Avenue, Room 300, Franklin, GA 30217; letters to P.O. Box 519(706) 675-3391Weekdays 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM
Board of Tax Assessors201 Park Avenue, Room 400, Franklin, GA 30217; letters to P.O. Box 476(706) 675-3786Weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, shut for lunch at noon until 1:00 PM

The Tax Commissioner's counter now stays open through lunch, a change that began September 1, 2026. Schedule an assessor visit outside the noon hour. The commissioner's email is heardtc@heardcountyga.com and the assessors answer at heardtax@heardcountyga.com.

Heard had 12,149 residents in July 2025, a 6.5% gain on the 2020 base of 11,410. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $186,800, and renters pay a median of $917 a month. There are 4,979 housing units and 4,309 households, and homeowners occupy 72.3% of homes.

Few households move in a given year, and only 54 permits were issued countywide in 2025. A listing here usually competes with older resale houses and country properties. Land area is 295.97 square miles, so many sales are rural parcels, and wooded tracts held for timber bring land-use questions that a Franklin city lot never raises.

sections.h2: Field visits and your property record
sections.html:
The assessors' office settles taxability, value and equalization, mails owners a notice when a value moves, and approves the exemptions people claim. Field staff visit each parcel to update the digest. They take a front photo and a rear photo of every structure and log changes since the previous countywide update. The state requires this cycle every three years.

Crews carry county identification and vehicle markings. A door hanger is left when nobody answers, so the owner can confirm the interior description. Before you list, phone (706) 675-3786 and ask what the card on your parcel says about bedrooms, baths, outbuildings and finished space. A garage that was converted years ago but still appears as a garage on the record can pull the value in the wrong direction, and a correction before the notice goes out costs you nothing.

  • The valuation date is January 1, and the taxable share is 40% of fair market value.
  • Parcel records are on the qpublic portal.
  • Returns of value are accepted from January 1 until April 1.

sections.h2: What to do if your value seems too high
sections.html:
Put your objection in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. You get 45 days counted from the mailing date on the notice, and the grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or an exemption the county denied. State revenue officials cannot override the county on one parcel, so the form should not go to Atlanta.

The uniform PT-311A form asks you to pick a route up front.

  • Board of Equalization: the common choice. The assessors can change the number and mail a fresh notice, which you may contest for another 30 days.
  • Hearing officer: reserved for non-homestead property above $500,000.
  • Arbitration: disputes over value alone, with a certified appraisal due 45 days after the board acknowledges your filing.

A dispute that survives can go on to superior court after written notice within 30 days of the ruling, and the previous year's tax has to be paid first. Complaints about the size of the bill are outside an appeal because elected bodies set the millage rate on their own.

House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, lets owners file a homestead application while the 45-day appeal window is open after assessment notices go out. The Assessor's Office takes it, and you should bring photo ID showing your current address. Skip the homestead filing on a house you live in and the exemption is treated as waived. April 1 is the usual deadline for a first-time filer.

The Board of Commissioners advertised in 2025 a tentative millage of 6.467 mills against a rollback figure of 5.467, which meant an 18.29 percent rise in collections. The Tax Commissioner's page posts a History of Tax Levy document for the year, which helps when you price a listing.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Heard County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on January 1 owes that year, and nothing is refunded to someone who sells early in the year. Read your bill or call (706) 675-3391 for the due date. The statewide default is December 20, though a county may pick December 1, November 15 or installment billing. Interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark on the bill.

Unpaid tax can lead to a recorded lien and then a public auction. After an auction, the owner has twelve months to redeem by paying the winning bid, later taxes and assessments, and a 20% premium. Anyone who inherits a house in that position should phone the commissioner early and get the payoff confirmed in writing.

A house with back taxes can still sell. The lien just has to be paid at the closing table, and the closing agent can wire the payoff straight to the commissioner.

  1. Call (706) 675-3391 and ask for a payoff figure on the parcel.
  2. Ask the assessors at (706) 675-3786 whether the property record matches the house as it stands.
  3. Give both numbers to the closing agent before signing day.
  4. If an auction has already happened, ask how much time is left to redeem.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so these four steps are most of the work. Bring a photo ID and your deed information to either office.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Heard County tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay at Room 300, 201 Park Avenue, Franklin, or send a check to P.O. Box 519, Franklin, GA 30217. The phone is (706) 675-3391. Weekday hours run 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, with no lunch closure since September 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Who decides what my Heard County house is worth?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors, in Room 400 at the same address, phone (706) 675-3786. The commissioner's office only bills, so value disputes go to the assessors.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to contest a Heard County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days beginning on the date the notice was mailed. A new notice opens a new window. File with the county assessors, not the state revenue department.

faqs.q: Can I add a Heard County homestead exemption after April 1?
faqs.a: Sometimes. House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, opened the 45-day appeal period after notices are mailed to homestead filings. Bring photo ID with your current address to the Assessor's Office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Heard County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the lien is paid off at the sale. Request a payoff figure from the closing agent before signing day. If an auction has already happened, twelve months are allowed to redeem at the bid plus a 20% premium and other charges.
